_comment: DATA-BACKFILL APPLY CHECKS. A migration whose whole effect is UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE declares no object, so its apply-state lives in the ROWS and no generic catalog check can read it. Each entry states how THAT file's effect is observed. kinds: evidence (ok = the file left a trace of itself -> APPLIED) · invariant (ok = the state it enforces holds today -> HOLDS; it cannot prove the file ran, only that nothing it fixed is broken) · superseded (a later migration rewrote the same rows) · unverifiable (ok = the reason still holds; false means this declaration is STALE and must be re-derived). `--self-test` FAILS if a data-only migration has no entry, an entry names a file that is not data-only, or a superseded_by file does not exist. First measured 2026-09-11 by hand, then declared here so nobody has to measure it again.

20260922b_not_stock_overrides_ship_empty.means: BOTH halves, because one file may carry one check and both are worth keeping: (1) none of the four rows 20260922 seeded for LAWNS remain — no migration-planted tenant data is left in the not-stock list; and (2) every active override still names the catalogue row its QuickBooks id points at, which is the check whose absence let 'Deposit' sit beside the id of 'Backyard Delivery'. Clause 2 holds vacuously while the list is empty and becomes load-bearing the moment an owner adds a row. ⚠️ A row an OWNER adds is legitimate and breaks neither clause: clause 1 names the four seeded ids, not the table's emptiness.
20260922b_not_stock_overrides_ship_empty.sql: (SELECT (SELECT count(*) = 0 FROM business_not_stock_items WHERE business_id = 'ed2e5933-45dc-4b9b-a331-ddfd125e7a74' AND qb_item_id IN ('603','1006','1007','1120')) AND (SELECT count(*) = 0 FROM business_not_stock_items o LEFT JOIN business_inventory i ON i.business_id = o.business_id AND i.qb_item_id = o.qb_item_id WHERE o.active AND (i.name IS NULL OR i.name NOT ILIKE '%' || o.item_name || '%')))

20260923g_manager_holds_order_discount_a.means: every MANAGER member row, and the system MANAGER floor, carries order_discount:apply — the two things this file UPDATEs. ledger #386, R-171 (a). ⚠️ It is `evidence` and not `invariant` because the floor could only have gained that string from this migration: before it, the floor held 25 strings without it (measured live 2026-09-23) and nothing else writes role_definitions
20260923g_manager_holds_order_discount_a.sql: ((SELECT bool_and(permissions ? 'order_discount:apply') FROM role_definitions WHERE role_key = 'MANAGER' AND business_id IS NULL AND is_system = true) AND (SELECT count(*) = 0 FROM business_members WHERE role = 'MANAGER' AND NOT (permissions ? 'order_discount:apply')))
